title: Hackers abuse Google Ads, Bing redirects to push Claude ClickFix attacks
key_facts: Push Security researchers found a malicious Google ad for the search "claude mac" that used a legitimate bing.com address.
The ad passed through Google's ad redirect, then a Bing click-tracking link, then a compromised WordPress site of a South American retailer, then the fake page claude-desk-code[.]com.
Cloaking meant visitors arriving directly were sent to a 404 page, hiding the payload from scanners.
The fake page shows Anthropic's genuine install command, but the copy button puts a different command on the clipboard.
That command decodes a hidden address, downloads a file from lake-90[.]com and runs it in the Mac terminal.
Push calls the technique "Adception" and tracks the ClickFix toolkit as AcSig.
quote_evidence: Hackers are abusing legitimate Bing search-result redirects as click URLs in Google search ads to direct users to fake Claude installers that deliver ClickFix attacks.
However, while the page displays Anthropic's legitimate installation command, curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash, clicking the copy button places a malicious command in the clipboard.
The final payload delivered by the attack remains unknown, so it unclear what malware, if any, is being installed.
why_it_matters_hint: Mac users searching for an AI tool can be tricked by a paid ad that looks safe.
notes: BleepingComputer relays a Push Security report; the Push report itself not read. Campaign start date not stated.
